title: Beans, cannellini, canned, sodium added, drained and rinsed

content.title: About
content.content: Cannellini beans are large white beans, also known as white kidney beans or navy beans. In canned form they often contain added salt. Draining and rinsing reduces the sodium content while preserving their mild nutty flavor and soft texture, making them ideal for salads, soups, and side dishes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Cannellini beans originate from the Mediterranean region and have been cultivated for over 2,000 years.
They are a rich source of plant protein and are frequently used in vegetarian meals as a meat substitute.
Canned beans are typically steam‑processed to retain nutrients.
Draining and rinsing canned beans can cut sodium levels by 30‑40 % compared with the original brine.
In Italy, cannellini beans are traditionally served with pasta, in pesto sauce, or in the classic dish "pasta e fagioli."

items.title: High in plant protein
items.content: A serving (about 130 g) provides roughly 15 g of protein, supporting muscle maintenance.

items.title: Rich in dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber promotes healthy digestion and helps maintain satiety.

items.title: Source of iron and folate
items.content: Iron is essential for oxygen transport, while folate supports DNA synthesis.

items.title: Low glycemic index
items.content: Beans raise blood sugar slowly, which is beneficial for glucose control.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Phytonutrients such as polyphenols help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Even after rinsing, canned beans may still contain notable amounts of salt, which can be problematic for hypertension.

items.title: Legume allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to beans.

items.title: Gas and bloating
items.content: Beans can cause gastrointestinal gas in sensitive people; introduce them gradually into the diet.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Drain and rinse the beans before use to reduce saltiness. Add them to salads, soups, stews, pasta dishes, pizza, or blend into hummus. They pair well with olive oil, garlic, herbs (rosemary, thyme) and a splash of lemon juice.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store unopened cans in a cool, dry place. After opening, transfer beans to an airtight container and keep refrigerated for up to 4‑5 days. Discard if an off‑odor or mold develops.
